chunks: And Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Yahya ibn Ishaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to the above.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a kunya for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْهَمْدَانِيُّ: Al-Hamdani, a nisba indicating lineage or tribe
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May God be pleased with him, a phrase of approval for a narrator
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Peace be upon him, honorific for the Imams
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ali ibn Ibrahim, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Similar to it, indicating the content matches a previously mentioned hadith

ai.seo_question: Who is the chain of narrators for the hadith about the ten characteristics of melons in Al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This isnad from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the rigorous transmission chain of the virtues of melons, linking the Prophet’s tradition through Ali ibn Ibrahim to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving practical sunnahs through a continuous line of trustworthy narrators, reinforcing the medicinal and spiritual benefits attributed to this fruit in early Islamic culture.
